examples.en: That actor is tall and handsome.

examples.ko: 훤칠한 청년이 가게 문을 열고 들어왔어요.
examples.en: A tall, good-looking young man opened the shop door and came in.
My son has grown up tall and good-looking, and it's nice to see.
I heard the groom is tall and handsome, and has a good personality too.

examples.ko: 새로 온 선생님은 훤칠해서 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: The new teacher stands out because he's tall and good-looking.

examples.ko: 저는 훤칠하지는 않아도 인상이 좋다는 말을 들어요.
examples.en: I may not be tall and striking, but people say I have a good impression.

explain: 키가 크면서 모습이 시원스럽고 보기 좋을 때 쓰는 칭찬이에요. '후리후리하다'는 키 크고 날씬한 몸을 말하고, '훤칠하다'는 거기에 잘생긴 느낌까지 더해져요. 주로 사람에게 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: He stepped onto the stage looking tall and handsome.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 시원스럽고 보기 좋은 외모를 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a person's tall, good-looking appearance.

phrases.en: You look even taller and more handsome in a suit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 그렇게 보인다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to compliment how someone appears.

phrases.en: My younger brother is tall and slender.
phrases.nuance_ko: 키 크고 날씬한 몸을 말해요. '훤칠하다'와 달리 잘생겼다는 느낌은 없어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a tall, slim build, without the good-looks sense of 훤칠하다.

explain_en: It is a compliment for someone who is tall and looks clean-cut and pleasing. '후리후리하다' describes a tall, slim body, while '훤칠하다' adds a handsome feel. It is used mainly for people.

examples.en: After Gyeongchip passed, the weather got much warmer.
They say frogs wake up on Gyeongchip.
This year Gyeongchip is in early March.
Around Gyeongchip, mornings and evenings are still chilly.

examples.ko: 경칩이 되면 겨울잠 자던 동물들이 깨어난다는 말이 있어요.
examples.en: There's a saying that animals that were hibernating wake up when Gyeongchip comes.

examples.ko: 달력에서 경칩이라는 글자를 보고 봄이 왔다고 느꼈어요.
examples.en: I saw the word Gyeongchip on the calendar and felt that spring had come.

explain: 24절기 중 하나로 '우수' 다음에 오고, 보통 3월 5일 무렵이에요. 개구리가 깨어난다는 이야기와 함께 봄이 온다는 느낌으로 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: Around Gyeongchip it is still chilly in the morning and evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날짜를 딱 정하지 않고 그즈음의 날씨나 분위기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the weather around that time without naming an exact date.

phrases.en: When Gyeongchip comes, frogs start to croak.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해마다 돌아오는 절기와 그때 일어나는 일을 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Links the yearly solar term with what happens at that time.

explain_en: It is one of the 24 solar terms, coming after '우수', and usually falls around March 5. People often mention it together with frogs waking up, as a sign that spring is arriving.

en: to be eventful; to be full of difficulties

examples.en: This year was truly an eventful one.
After two eventful years, I am finally graduating.
Our family history has really been full of ups and downs.
The wedding preparations were so eventful that I was overwhelmed.

examples.ko: 다사다난하게 보낸 한 해를 정리해 봤어요.
examples.en: I looked back over the eventful year I went through.
It had its share of trouble, but it was an enjoyable trip.

explain: 연말 인사나 뉴스에서 '다사다난했던 한 해'라고 자주 말해요. 단순히 바쁜 게 아니라 일도 많고 어려움도 있었다는 느낌이라 '바쁘다'와 달라요. 주로 한 해, 시절, 인생 같은 긴 시간에 써요.

phrases.en: I had an eventful year this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연말 인사에서 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in year-end greetings.

phrases.en: The past few years have been really eventful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체 과거형으로 지난 시간을 돌아볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite past form, used when looking back on a period of time.

phrases.en: My grandmother lived a life full of ups and downs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인생처럼 긴 시간에 일도 어려움도 많았다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a long span like a life that held many events and hardships.

explain_en: People often say '다사다난했던 한 해' in year-end greetings and news. It is not just 'busy': it means many things happened, including difficulties. It is mainly used for long periods such as a year, an era or a life.

en: the three hottest periods of summer (chobok, jungbok, malbok)

examples.en: Many people eat samgyetang during sambok.

examples.ko: 올해는 삼복 내내 비가 자주 왔어요.
examples.en: This year it rained often throughout the sambok period.
After sambok passed, the mornings and evenings became cool.

examples.ko: 삼복의 더위를 이기려고 시원한 수박을 먹어요.
examples.en: I eat cold watermelon to beat the heat of sambok.

examples.ko: 삼복 중에 가장 더운 때는 언제예요?
examples.en: When is the hottest time within sambok?
It's hard to get by without air conditioning during sambok.

explain: 초복, 중복, 말복을 합쳐 부르는 한여름 더위의 시기예요. 보통 '삼복더위'라고 붙여 말하는 일이 많고, 이 시기에는 삼계탕 같은 보양식을 먹는 문화가 있어요.

phrases.en: Don't stay outside long in the dog days of summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '삼복'보다 더 자주 쓰는 말로, 한여름의 심한 더위를 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common than 삼복 alone; it means the intense heat of midsummer.

phrases.example: 삼복 동안에는 시원한 음식을 많이 먹어요.
phrases.en: During the sambok period, I eat a lot of cool food.
phrases.nuance_ko: 초복부터 말복까지의 기간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the whole period from chobok to malbok.

phrases.en: My family eats health-boosting food during sambok.
phrases.nuance_ko: 삼복의 대표적인 풍습을 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the typical sambok custom.

explain_en: The whole three-Bok hottest period of summer, not one day. It refers to the three hottest days of midsummer together: 초복, 중복 and 말복. It is often said as '삼복더위', and people traditionally eat energy-boosting food such as samgyetang then.

en: occasionally; by chance; once in a while

examples.en: Drop by whenever you're passing. You're always welcome.
I got to know that person just by running into them now and then.
When we run into each other, we greet each other warmly.
My brother and I do argue from time to time.

examples.ko: 오다가다 눈에 띄는 가게라서 한번 들어가 봤어요.
examples.en: It was a shop I kept noticing as I passed by, so I went in once.
I've seen the face around, but I don't know the name.

explain: '오고 가는 도중에'라는 뜻에서 나와, 특별한 약속 없이 우연히나 가끔 일어나는 일에 써요. '자주'보다는 가볍고 우연한 느낌이에요. '오다가다 만난 사이'는 깊지 않은 인연을 말할 때 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I ran into that person now and then.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속 없이 우연히 자주는 아니게 만날 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for meeting someone by chance, without plans, and not very often.

phrases.en: I heard that story here and there.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 찾지 않았는데 우연히 들었다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests you heard it by chance without looking for it.

phrases.en: Please come visit sometimes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오다가다'와 비슷하지만 더 일반적이고 우연의 느낌은 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 오다가다 but more general, with less sense of chance.

explain_en: Now and then while passing by, casual encounters (오다가다) It comes from 'on the way coming and going' and is used for things that happen by chance or now and then, without any plan. It feels lighter and more incidental than '자주'. '오다가다 만난 사이' is a common way to describe a casual acquaintance.

t90.ax: My brother and I do argue from time to time.

examples.en: In my day, I was a soccer player too.

examples.ko: 우리 할아버지는 왕년에 꽤 유명한 가수였대요.
examples.en: They say my grandfather was a fairly famous singer back in the day.

examples.ko: 왕년의 인기 배우가 오랜만에 드라마에 나와요.
examples.en: A once-popular actor is appearing in a drama after a long time.

examples.ko: 왕년에 날리던 실력이 아직 남아 있는지 보여 줄게요.
examples.en: I'll show you whether the skills I had in my heyday are still there.

examples.ko: 아빠는 왕년에 이 동네에서 제일 잘나갔다고 자랑해요.
examples.en: Dad brags that he was the top guy in this neighborhood in his day.

examples.ko: 왕년 얘기만 하지 말고 지금 이야기를 해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't just talk about the old days; let's talk about now.

explain: 그냥 '옛날'이 아니라 내가 잘나가던 시절, 한창 좋았던 때를 말할 때 써요. 그래서 '왕년에 내가 말이야'처럼 약간 자랑하거나 농담하는 말투로 자주 나와요. 거의 '왕년에' 꼴로 쓰고, 지금은 그때만 못하다는 느낌이 깔려 있기도 해요.

phrases.en: A former star appeared on TV after a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한창 잘나가던 시절의 유명인을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a celebrity from their heyday.

phrases.en: I still have my old skills.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예전에 잘하던 능력을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the ability someone once had at their peak.

phrases.example: 아버지는 늘 '왕년에 내가 말이야' 하고 말을 시작하세요.
phrases.en: Dad always starts with 'Back in my day...'.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거를 자랑하거나 농담할 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A boastful or joking way to start talking about the past.

explain_en: It is not just 'the past' but one's glory days, when things were going well. That is why it often appears in a boastful or joking tone, as in '왕년에 내가 말이야'. It is mostly used as '왕년에', and it often implies that things are not as good now.

examples.en: My father was born in the year of the rat.
I was born in the same year as my friend who is a rat.
They say people born in the year of the rat are diligent.
My younger sibling is a rat and I'm an ox.
I hear this year is lucky for those born in the year of the rat.
The people born in the year of the rat formed a group.

explain: 한국에서는 '무슨 띠예요?'라고 물으면 '쥐띠예요'처럼 태어난 해의 동물로 대답해요. 다른 띠도 '소띠', '호랑이띠'처럼 '띠'가 붙어요. 나이를 직접 묻지 않고 대략 알아볼 때도 써요.

phrases.en: What's your zodiac animal? I'm a rat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 띠를 물어보는 질문이고, 대답에 '쥐띠예요'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A question about your zodiac animal; answer with 쥐띠예요.

phrases.en: People born in the year of the rat gathered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쥐의 해라는 것을 말할 때 '해'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 해 to mean the year of the rat.

phrases.en: I was born in the year of the rat and my younger sibling in the year of the ox.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 띠와 함께 비교해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when comparing with another zodiac animal.

explain_en: In Korea, when asked '무슨 띠예요?' you answer with your birth-year animal, like '쥐띠예요'. Other signs work the same way, such as '소띠' and '호랑이띠'. People also use it to get a rough idea of someone's age without asking directly.

examples.en: That rumor became the gossip topic at the company.
Celebrity weddings are always gossip material.
Please don't make me into gossip.
All we talked about at lunch was gossip.
Something like this doesn't end as mere gossip.
I don't want to become gossip among my friends.

explain: '입방아에 오르다'와 비슷하게, 사람들이 재미로 말하는 소문이나 남의 사생활 이야기를 가리켜요. 보통 좋지 않은 느낌이라 '가십거리가 되다'는 남의 입에 오르내린다는 말이에요. 중립적인 '이야깃거리'와 달라요.

phrases.en: Don't make other people's business a topic of gossip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 이야기를 재미로 말하는 것을 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to discourage turning others' affairs into gossip.

phrases.en: There is a lot of gossip in that neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소문이 많이 도는 곳이나 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a place or person with lots of rumors.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a lot of gossip

phrases.example: 새로 온 직원이 점심시간 이야깃거리가 됐어요.
phrases.en: The new employee became a topic of conversation at lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 느낌 없이 중립적으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A neutral word without a negative feel.

explain_en: Like '입방아에 오르다', it refers to rumors or other people's private lives that people talk about for fun. It usually has a negative feel, so '가십거리가 되다' means to become the subject of people's talk. It differs from the neutral '이야깃거리' (a topic to talk about).

en: to be despicable; to be detestable

examples.en: The way he pretends to be kind only on the surface is detestable.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 가증스러운 거짓말에 모두 화가 났어요.
examples.en: Everyone was angry at that person's despicable lie.

examples.ko: 자기가 잘못해 놓고 남 탓을 하다니 정말 가증스럽네요.
examples.en: Blaming others after doing wrong yourself is really despicable.

examples.ko: 웃으면서 뒤에서 욕하는 게 가증스럽지 않아요?
examples.en: Isn't it despicable to smile and then curse behind someone's back?
I still remember his detestable excuse.

examples.ko: 가증스럽게 눈물을 흘리는 모습에 다들 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Everyone was shocked to see him shed hypocritical tears.

explain: 거짓되고 위선적인 모습이 밉고 역겨울 때 쓰는 센 표현이에요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '가증스러워요', '가증스러운'으로 바뀌어요. 가볍게 얄미울 때는 '얄밉다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 가증스러운 행동을 보고 정말 화가 났어요.
phrases.en: I got really angry when I saw that despicable behavior.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 모양이에요. 위선적인 행동이나 말에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form that modifies a noun, used for hypocritical acts or words.

phrases.en: That person's smile is detestable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 말할 때의 모양이에요. 웃음이나 태도가 가짜 같아서 역겨울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form, used when a smile or attitude seems fake and disgusting.

phrases.en: He lied while smiling in a despicable way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 앞에서 행동하는 모습을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form, describing the way someone does an action.

explain_en: This is a strong expression for hypocrisy or falseness that feels hateful and disgusting. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '가증스러워요' and '가증스러운'. For mild annoyance, '얄밉다' sounds more natural.

en: being on bad terms; like dog and monkey

examples.en: The presidents of the two companies have been at odds for a long time.
My brother and I have been like cats and dogs since we were kids.

examples.ko: 그 두 사람이 견원지간인 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I did not know those two were sworn enemies.

examples.ko: 견원지간처럼 싸우던 두 팀이 드디어 화해했어요.
examples.en: The two teams that fought like cat and dog finally made up.

examples.ko: 시어머니와 며느리를 견원지간으로 보는 건 편견이에요.
examples.en: Seeing a mother-in-law and daughter-in-law as enemies is a prejudice.

examples.ko: 두 이웃은 견원지간이라서 서로 인사도 안 해요.
examples.en: The two neighbors are bitter enemies, so they don't even greet each other.

explain: 개와 원숭이처럼 만나면 으르렁대는 사이를 빗댄 사자성어예요. 한자는 犬(개 견), 猿(원숭이 원)을 써요. 보통 '두 사람은 견원지간이다'처럼 사이를 말할 때 쓰고, '앙숙'은 서로 미워하는 상대 자체를 가리킬 때도 써요. 반대로 아주 친한 사이는 '단짝'이나 '죽마고우'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The two are sworn enemies who fight whenever they meet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 미워하는 상대 자체를 가리킬 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can refer to the hated rival themselves.

phrases.en: The two families have been on bad terms for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '견원지간' 대신 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday talk, people say this instead of 견원지간.

phrases.en: The two countries have long been bitter enemies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사이가 아주 나쁜 두 사람이나 집단을 말할 때 '이다'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '이다' to describe two people or groups whose relationship is very bad.

explain_en: A four-character idiom comparing two sides to a dog and a monkey that snarl whenever they meet. The characters are 犬 (dog) and 猿 (monkey). It usually describes the relationship, as in '두 사람은 견원지간이다', while '앙숙' can also refer to the hated rival themselves. For very close friends, say '단짝' or '죽마고우'.

examples.en: Wicked stepmothers often appear in old tales.
I get along well with my stepmother.
Cinderella's stepmother tormented Cinderella.

examples.ko: 그는 어릴 때 계모 밑에서 자랐어요.
examples.en: He grew up with a stepmother as a child.

examples.ko: 계모라는 말에는 나쁜 인상이 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: The word stepmother carries a bad image.

examples.ko: 드라마 속 계모는 사실 따뜻한 사람이었어요.
examples.en: The stepmother in the drama was actually a warm person.

explain: 아버지의 새 아내를 가리키는 말이에요. 옛이야기 때문에 부정적인 이미지가 있어서, 실제로 부르거나 소개할 때는 '새어머니'를 더 많이 써요. 어머니의 새 남편은 '계부'이고, 일상에서는 '새아버지'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I live with my stepmother.
phrases.nuance_ko: '계모'보다 부드럽고 존중하는 말이라 실제로 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer and more respectful than 계모, used when introducing someone.

phrases.en: My stepmom made me a delicious meal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구어체로 친근하게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A friendly, spoken form.

phrases.en: My mother remarried, so I got a stepfather.
phrases.nuance_ko: '계모'와 짝이 되는 말로, 어머니의 새 남편이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counterpart of 계모: mother's new husband.

explain_en: Stepmother in written or fairy-tale use, often negative image. It refers to a father's new wife. Because of old tales it has a negative image, so in real life people prefer 새어머니 when calling or introducing her. A mother's new husband is 계부, and in daily speech 새아버지.

t90.ax: I get along well with my stepmother.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 성격 궁합이 아주 잘 맞아요.
examples.en: The two of them are very compatible in personality.

examples.ko: 결혼 전에 궁합을 보는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people have their compatibility read before marriage.
This sauce and meat go really well together.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 호흡이 잘 맞고 궁합도 좋아요.
examples.en: Our team works well together and has good chemistry.

examples.ko: 제 피부와 이 크림은 궁합이 안 맞는 것 같아요.
examples.en: This cream doesn't seem to suit my skin.

examples.ko: 이번 신입 직원과 선배는 궁합이 어때요?
examples.en: How is the chemistry between this new employee and the senior?

explain: 원래는 두 사람의 생년월일로 결혼 상대와 어울리는지 보는 풍습이에요. 지금은 사람뿐 아니라 음식, 색, 물건이 잘 어울릴 때도 '궁합이 좋다/맞다'라고 해요. 반대는 '궁합이 안 맞다'예요.

phrases.en: These two foods go well together.
phrases.nuance_ko: '궁합이 맞다'와 비슷하게 잘 어울릴 때 쓰고, 사람뿐 아니라 음식이나 물건에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 'gunghap matda'; used when things match well, for people, food, or objects.

phrases.example: 저와 제 룸메이트는 궁합이 안 맞아요.
phrases.en: My roommate and I are not compatible.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘 어울리지 않을 때 쓰는 반대 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite expression, used when two things or people do not fit well.

phrases.en: Kimchi and pork belly are a great food pairing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 먹으면 맛있거나 몸에 좋은 음식 짝을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for food pairs that taste good or are healthy together.

explain_en: It began as a custom of checking a couple's match from their birth dates. Today people also say 궁합이 좋다 or 궁합이 맞다 for foods, colors and objects that go well together. The opposite is 궁합이 안 맞다.

en: to be pushy; to be overzealous

examples.en: That family's kid is really hyper and pushy.
The child is having a hard time because of overbearing parents.
Our puppy runs around in such a wild way.

examples.ko: 동생이 극성맞게 졸라서 결국 사 줬어요.
examples.en: My little brother pestered me so relentlessly that I ended up buying it.

examples.ko: 극성맞은 팬들이 가수 집 앞에서 기다렸어요.
examples.en: Obsessive fans waited in front of the singer's house.

examples.ko: 극성맞게 굴지 말고 얌전히 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: Don't be so wild; sit still and behave.

explain: 성격이 드세고 지나치게 열심이거나 부산스러운 사람이나 동물에게 써요. 칭찬보다는 조금 못마땅한 느낌이 있어요. 비슷하게 '극성스럽다'도 써요.

phrases.en: The children play wildly and noisily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사형으로 쓰면 행동이 드세고 정신없는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: As an adverb, it describes behavior that is rowdy and hectic.

phrases.en: That puppy is really hyper.
phrases.nuance_ko: '극성맞다'와 뜻이 비슷하고 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning to 극성맞다 and can be swapped with it.

phrases.en: My son isn't rowdy; he is quiet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 쓰면 얌전하다는 뜻을 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form can say that someone is calm and well-behaved.

explain_en: It describes people or animals that are pushy, overly zealous or restless. It carries a slightly disapproving feeling rather than praise. '극성스럽다' is used in a similar way.

t90.ax: Don't be so wild; sit still and behave.

en: to be polite; to be properly respectful

examples.ko: 후배는 선배에게 깍듯이 인사하는 것이 습관이 됐어요.
examples.en: Greeting seniors politely has become a habit for the junior.

examples.ko: 그 가게 직원들은 손님에게 깍듯이 대해서 단골이 많아요.
examples.en: The staff at that shop treat customers so courteously that they have many regulars.

examples.ko: 민수 씨는 어른들 앞에서 늘 예의가 깍듯해요.
examples.en: Minsu is always very well-mannered in front of his elders.

examples.ko: 깍듯한 태도 덕분에 면접관에게 좋은 인상을 줬어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my courteous attitude, I made a good impression on the interviewer.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 친구 부모님께도 깍듯하게 말해요.
examples.en: My younger brother speaks respectfully even to his friends' parents.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말투가 깍듯해서 처음에는 조금 어려웠어요.
examples.en: His way of speaking was so formal that he felt a little hard to approach at first.

explain: 예의를 빈틈없이 지키는 모습에 써요. 주로 윗사람이나 손님을 대하는 태도를 말할 때 어울려요. '깍듯이 인사하다'처럼 부사형으로도 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 새로 온 직원은 태도가 깍듯해서 인상이 좋아요.
phrases.en: The new employee has a polite manner, so they make a good impression.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 예의 바른 모습을 칭찬할 때 써요. 윗사람에게 하는 행동에 특히 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise someone's good manners, especially toward superiors.

phrases.example: 그 식당 직원은 손님을 항상 깍듯하게 대해요.
phrases.en: The staff at that restaurant always treat customers courteously.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여 사람을 대하는 방식을 말해요. '깍듯이 대하다'로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-게' it describes how someone treats others. '깍듯이 대하다' works too.

phrases.en: That student is polite to adults.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말이에요. '예의 바르다'는 일반적으로 예의가 좋다는 뜻이고, '깍듯하다'는 빈틈없이 정중하다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word. '예의 바르다' means well-mannered in general, while '깍듯하다' feels more flawlessly proper.

explain_en: Strictly proper manners, esp. toward elders or seniors. It describes someone who keeps good manners without any slack, mostly in how they treat elders or customers. It fits attitudes toward people of higher status. It is also used as the adverb form, as in '깍듯이 인사하다'.
